01 Add your angles

5–20 seconds each

Film at a steady pace, with your whole body visible. Use a fixed camera at hip height, ideally 60 fps or higher.

How to get a useful recording +

Use a true side view for cadence and torso tilt. Front and rear views show projected pelvis motion. Keep the camera level and stationary; avoid wide-angle distortion. Wear contrasting clothing and keep feet in frame. Record normal-speed video, not slow motion. If you film different takes, use the same pace and conditions. Independent clips cannot reconstruct synchronized 3D movement.

Add at least one video to get started.

YOUR SESSION

Observations, then experiments.

Export data for model validation

Download timestamped skeleton coordinates, recording dimensions and observations. The file contains movement data, but no video or original filenames. It stays local unless you choose to share it.

Leave unchecked to export unlabelled pose data. Use a pseudonymous runner code, consistently across sessions, so validation can keep runners separate from training data. This does not train a model or create an economy prediction.

THE ECONOMY QUESTION

Movement tells part of the story.

Running economy is the oxygen or energy cost of running at a given speed. Video can describe your mechanics, but this prototype has no validated model for estimating your metabolic cost or a percentage improvement.

A lab test with steady-state gas exchange is needed to assess actual running economy. Heart rate alone is not a substitute.

BUILT ON EVIDENCE · REVIEWED NOVEMBER 2026

No universal perfect stride.

01 / SYSTEMATIC REVIEW · 2024

Mechanics and economy are related. The relationship is individual.

Observational associations do not prove that changing one metric will improve your economy.

Markerless tracking needs validation for each measurement.

OpenCap research supports the promise of video analysis. Its validation does not transfer automatically to this app or MediaPipe.

Read the research ↗03 / NARRATIVE REVIEW · 2026

180 steps per minute is not a universal target.
